title: New Global Fund Replenishment Data Now Available
author: GADH Team
excerpt: We have updated our replenishment tracker with the latest figures from the Geneva negotiations, including breakdowns by donor country and disease allocation.
content:
We have updated our replenishment tracker with the latest figures from the Geneva negotiations, including breakdowns by donor country and disease allocation.

## What's New

The updated dataset covers pledges from 42 contributing countries, with particular detail on how allocations are split between HIV, tuberculosis, and malaria programmes.

> This data is critical for communities who need to hold donors accountable to their commitments.

## How to Access the Data

Visit our Resources page to download the full dataset as a CSV or explore it interactively through our dashboard.

title: Community Voices from the Board Meeting
author: Advocacy Team
excerpt: Representatives from 12 community delegations shared their priorities at the May board meeting. Here is a summary of the key themes that emerged.
content:
Representatives from 12 community delegations shared their priorities at the May board meeting. Here is a summary of the key themes that emerged.

## Key Themes

Delegations consistently raised concerns around grant implementation delays, community systems strengthening funding, and the need for more transparent reporting from Principal Recipients.

## Next Steps

The GADH team will be publishing a full briefing note with recommendations for the next board cycle. Sign up to our mailing list to receive it directly.

title: Understanding the Country Coordinating Mechanism
author: Research Team
excerpt: A plain-language guide to how CCMs work, who sits on them, and how communities can engage with the process to influence funding decisions.
content:
The Country Coordinating Mechanism, or CCM, is the national body responsible for overseeing Global Fund grants. Understanding how it works is essential for community advocates.

## Who Sits on a CCM?

CCMs include representatives from government ministries, civil society organisations, the private sector, and communities living with or affected by the three diseases.

## How Decisions Are Made

Grant applications, implementation plans, and oversight reports all pass through the CCM. Communities with a seat at the table can directly influence these documents.

> The most impactful advocacy often happens before a grant is submitted, not after it is approved.
